retained_findings.description: Easy banks always contain {t,-t,b,-b,0}, with |t|>|b|. If the numeric coefficient signs agree, choose the largest positive option; otherwise choose the most negative option. This skips the required magnitude calculation and answers every delivered batch item. Five stored generated questions have the same defect.
Source q-74691 requires fractional elimination with a bare parameter coefficient. Its profile is missing, and existing hard-template constraints exclude its parameters.
Default banks contain both t and -t, so every valid t=0 case collides and is rejected or resampled away.

Finite batch-selection failure: both opposite-sign items repeat one coefficient decision and make the smallest option correct. Changed RHS values and bank spacing preserve the shortcut throughout this recognizable subgroup.
Five captured historical v2 easy records retain the sign-only extremum shortcut and remain learner-selection candidates. Their unresolved presence prevents a passing delivered-distribution claim.

assessment: Three initial independent strict tests fail old code with the stated bank collision, unknown profile and 48/48 shortcut; all pass current code.

Author source regression fails old code first on missing bank_variant metadata; this is not evidence of the missing-source defect. Independent acceptance-tests.py separately reproduces Unknown profile at q-74691.

Prior five-item batch and two exact negative subgroup members reproduce the old finite-pool failure. Current CLI and runner batch pass the independently parsed contrasts; single-seed old counterexamples remain replayable.
Current inventory replays all five old defective records but excludes them through explicit retirement. Historical defect is preserved in generated-records.json; no eligible affected record remains.

Strict historical inventory check also fails on a local negative control with only the five retirement flags reset: affected=5 and shortcut=64/64. It passes actual captured basis 5575 with affected=0.
